summary: New Zealand Police publish child sexual assault, child assault, abuse-material and grooming victims, and the people proceeded against, by ethnicity every month, with European separate from Māori, Pacific and Asian people. It is the only country reviewed so far whose official crime data separately identify European-descent victims and offenders. Gaps: many child victims have no recorded ethnicity, offenders are not split by victim age outside child-specific offences, there is no victim-by-offender ethnicity table, and child-protection data lump NZ European with Other.

nations.National (NZ Police): Recorded Crime Victims and Offenders Statistics by ethnicity, monthly since July 2014; homicide victims report.
nations.Oranga Tamariki: Child-protection data with prioritised ethnicity (Māori, Pacific, NZ European & Other).

european_note: NZ Police record 'European' (NZ European and other European ethnicities) as its own group for victims and for people proceeded against, alongside Māori, Pacific, Asian, Indian and other groups. Oranga Tamariki child-protection data instead lump NZ European with Other.

harms.label: Sexual assault of a child (police)
harms.intro: Police recorded 3417 victimisations of sexual assault of a child in 2025 (1690 with the victim recorded as aged 0-14), and proceeded against offenders 856 times. Both victims and offenders are published by ethnicity, with European separate.

victims.scope: New Zealand, victimisations of sexual assault of a child, victims aged 0-14, 2025
victims.rate_label: victimisations per 100,000 children aged 0-14 of the same ethnic group
victims.rate_note: Calculated here: police counts divided by 2023 Census usually resident population (Stats NZ, total-response ethnicity). Police record one ethnicity per person while the census counts people in every group they identify with, so these rates are approximate (groups with many multi-ethnic people, such as Māori and Pacific, are understated less than they would be with single-ethnicity denominators). The all-groups rate includes people whose ethnicity was not stated.
victims.share_note: NZ Police record one ethnicity per person (European, Māori, Pacific, Asian, Indian, African, Latin American, Middle Eastern, other). 'European' covers NZ European and other European ethnicities, so European-descent people are separately identified. Asian here includes the police 'Indian' category (shown separately too); 'Middle Eastern, Latin American or African' combines three police categories. Victimisations count a victim once per incident and offence type. Excludes incidents later found to be 'no crime'.

perpetrators.scope: New Zealand, police proceedings for sexual assault of a child, offenders of all ages, 2025
perpetrators.rate_label: proceedings per 100,000 residents of the same ethnic group (all ages)
perpetrators.rate_note: Calculated here: police counts divided by 2023 Census usually resident population (Stats NZ, total-response ethnicity). Police record one ethnicity per person while the census counts people in every group they identify with, so these rates are approximate (groups with many multi-ethnic people, such as Māori and Pacific, are understated less than they would be with single-ethnicity denominators). The all-groups rate includes people whose ethnicity was not stated.
perpetrators.share_note: NZ Police record one ethnicity per person (European, Māori, Pacific, Asian, Indian, African, Latin American, Middle Eastern, other). 'European' covers NZ European and other European ethnicities, so European-descent people are separately identified. Asian here includes the police 'Indian' category (shown separately too); 'Middle Eastern, Latin American or African' combines three police categories. Counts proceedings (a person proceeded against on a day), not unique people or convictions. The offence itself means the victim was a child. 147 of the 856 proceedings were against people aged 10-19.

cross.text: Police publish the offender's relationship to the victim, but not the offender's ethnicity alongside the victim's, so no victim-by-offender ethnicity table exists.

harms.label: Neglect, and harm to children in state care
harms.intro: New Zealand publishes no national count of neglect findings by ethnicity. Oranga Tamariki reports how many children in state care were found to have been harmed (any abuse or neglect) by ethnicity, lumping NZ European with Other. Police proceeded against offenders for neglect or ill-treatment of a person under care 77 times in 2025.

harms.label: Homicide
harms.intro: Police counted 1174 homicide victims from 2007 to 2022, of whom 152 were under 15 (123 under 5). Victims are published by ethnicity (European 405, Māori 372) but not by ethnicity and age together. Police proceeded against offenders for murder or manslaughter 135 times in 2025, published by ethnicity.

Ethnicity is not published by age, so child victims cannot be split by ethnicity. 2019 includes the 51 victims of the Christchurch mosque attacks.

breakdown.why: NZ Police publish victims of 'sexual assault of a child' and people proceeded against for it by ethnicity, with European separate from Māori, Pacific, Asian and other groups, updated monthly. Victim ethnicity is not stated for about a quarter of victimisations; offender ethnicity unknown for about 13%. Police record one ethnicity per person and the method is not fully documented. No victim-by-offender ethnicity table.

Assault victims aged 0-14 by ethnicity (European separate), including assaults by a family member; ethnicity not stated for 46% of child assault victimisations. Offender ethnicity exists only for all assaults, not split by the victim's age.

People proceeded against for neglect or ill-treatment of a person under care by ethnicity (European separate; includes vulnerable adults). Victims: only Oranga Tamariki's count of children harmed in state care, which lumps 'NZ European & Other'.

Police homicide victims report gives victims by ethnicity (European separate) and by age, but not ethnicity by age; final data end in 2022. People proceeded against for murder and manslaughter by ethnicity (2025), all victims. No rates or victim-offender ethnicity link published.
No victim data. 45 police proceedings for human trafficking or slavery since mid-2014 by offender ethnicity, all forms and ages.

Victims and offenders of child abuse material and child grooming offences by ethnicity (European separate). Most victims in abuse material are unidentified (41% of victimisations have no ethnicity), and cases prosecuted by Internal Affairs or Customs are not in police data.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify children of European descent (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump European-descent people with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, European descent separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies people of European descent, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when European-descent children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: New Zealand scores 44% on the stricter scale (40-60%), the first country reviewed whose police data separately identify European victims and European offenders. NZ Police publish child sexual assault victims and the people proceeded against for it by ethnicity every month. It loses points because a quarter to half of child victims have no recorded ethnicity, offenders are not split by the victim's age outside child-specific offences, there is no victim-by-offender ethnicity table, and child-protection data lump NZ European with Other.
score.judgement_notes: Police ethnicity is treated as real ethnicity data with European descent separately identified, even though police record a single ethnicity and the method (self-identified or officer-recorded) is not documented in the release. If police ethnicity were treated as perceived and docked like US offender race, NZ would score about 38% (every police-based heritage score cut by a fifth).

nzp_vic.name: policedata.nz: Victimisations (demographics), Recorded Crime Victims Statistics
nzp_vic.years: Monthly, July 2014 to September 2026 (workbook downloaded 18 Nov 2026)
nzp_vic.records: Victimisations by ANZSOC 2023 offence (including sexual assault of a child, assault, child abuse material and grooming), victim age group, sex, ethnicity and offender relationship.
nzp_vic.limitations: One police-recorded ethnicity per victim; 'not stated' is common for child victims. Excludes homicide and offences without a specific victim. No offender ethnicity in the victim data.

nzp_off.name: policedata.nz: Proceedings (offender demographics), Recorded Crime Offenders Statistics
nzp_off.years: Monthly, July 2014 to September 2026 (workbook downloaded 18 Nov 2026)
nzp_off.records: Police proceedings by ANZSOC 2023 offence, offender age group, sex, ethnicity and method of proceeding.
nzp_off.limitations: Counts proceedings, not unique offenders or convictions; not split by the victim's age except where the offence is child-specific. One police-recorded ethnicity.

nzp_hom.name: Homicide Victims Report 2023
nzp_hom.records: Homicide victims by year, gender, age group, ethnicity and relationship to offender.
nzp_hom.limitations: Ethnicity and age are not cross-tabulated; 'Other/Unknown' is one category; no offender ethnicity.

census23.name: 2023 Census population counts by ethnic group, age and Māori descent (Table 9)
census23.records: Usually resident population by ethnic group (total responses, level 1) and five-year age group.
census23.limitations: Total-response ethnicity (people counted in each group they identify with), unlike police single ethnicity; used here only as rate denominators.

ot_ar25.name: Oranga Tamariki Annual Report 2024/25: Safety of Children in Care appendix
ot_ar25.records: Children in care with findings of harm, by prioritised ethnicity, age and gender, and the people believed responsible by role.
ot_ar25.limitations: Children in state care only; 'NZ European & Other' lumps European with all other non-Māori, non-Pacific children; no ethnicity of the people responsible.

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
